verdict.rationale: Kong Gateway's Vault entity lets you store secrets and reference them from other entities, so secrets are not visible in plaintext across the platform. Secrets can come from environment variables, the Konnect Config Store, or a supported third-party backend vault, which directly covers the external-vault half of the story. Missing for 10: named list of supported third-party vault backends, explicit evidence that decK/declarative config files use vault references instead of raw credentials, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can keep credentials out of shared files with masked secrets or an external vault integration

citations.quote: Vaults allow you to securely store and then reference secrets from within other entities, ensuring that secrets aren't visible in plaintext throughout the platform.
You can add secrets to Vaults in one of the following ways: * Environment variables * Konnect Config Store * Supported third-party backend vault
